results.original_concern: Proof 4.2 says that m has abelianization -1 under x↦q,y↦p, 'so it is opposite the positive normal-disk meridian, whose class is the positive generator by [F3].' F3 establishes generation by the geometric positive meridian, but does not calibrate its sign against this newly chosen algebraic isomorphism to Z. Proof 5.1 currently refers back to 4.2 for that calibration.
results.reason: F3 proves that the geometric positive meridian generates exterior homology but allows either isomorphism of that infinite cyclic group with Z. Hence it cannot justify the sign under the separately chosen map x↦q,y↦p. The sign is essential to the stated oriented meridian word and longitude exponent, and step 5.1 relies on 4.2 for precisely this calibration. The proposed hemispherical-disk calculation supplies the missing sign directly for either sign of p and q, including absolute value one, without changing the theorem.

proposals.source_excerpt: Its abelianization under $x\mapsto q$, $y\mapsto p$ is $cq-dp=-1$, so it is opposite the positive normal-disk meridian, whose class is the positive generator by [F3].
proposals.proposed_replacement: To calibrate signs geometrically, the positively oriented coordinate cores representing $x$ and $y$ bound the hemispherical disks $D_x=\{\operatorname{Im}z_2=0,\ \operatorname{Re}z_2\ge0\}\cap S^3$ and $D_y=\{\operatorname{Im}z_1=0,\ \operatorname{Re}z_1\ge0\}\cap S^3$, oriented by their respective core boundaries. The knot meets $D_x$ transversely in $|q|$ points, each with intersection sign $\operatorname{sgn}(q)$, and meets $D_y$ in $|p|$ points, each with sign $\operatorname{sgn}(p)$. For the first sign, at a point where $z_2$ is positive real, the ambient orientation is the complex $z_1$ orientation followed by increasing $\operatorname{Im}z_2$; the component of the knot tangent transverse to $D_x$ has sign $q$. For the second, at positive real $z_1$, the ambient orientation is increasing $\operatorname{Im}z_1$ followed by the complex $z_2$ orientation, and the transverse tangent component has sign $p$. Deleting small disks about these intersections gives oriented surfaces in the knot complement with boundary relations $[x]=q[\mu]$ and $[y]=p[\mu]$, where $\mu$ is the positive normal-disk meridian. Thus the abelianization $x\mapsto q$, $y\mapsto p$ sends this geometric meridian to $1$: [F3] makes $[\mu]$ a generator, and the displayed relations and $\gcd(p,q)=1$ fix its sign. The disk-boundary curve $m$ has abelianization $cq-dp=-1$, so its orientation is opposite to that positive meridian.
